summary: Describes a Uniform Resource Name namespace for the Digital Video Broadcasting project, used for naming persistent resources defined in its standards. These include technical documents, XML schemas, classification schemes, DTDs, namespaces, style sheets, and media assets. It is informational and was later updated.

plainLanguage.summary: Each book in a library needs a permanent call number. This gives the digital television standards group a naming system so its documents and files can always be found by name.

questions: what is the urn dvb namespace
how are urn dvb names resolved
subtitle: How the DVB Project registered the urn:dvb namespace to name its standards, schemas and metadata.

tldr.problem: The Digital Video Broadcasting Project (DVB) wants unique, permanent, location-independent names for resources such as XML schemas and classification schemes.
tldr.mechanism: It registers the formal URN namespace ID dvb, with names of the form urn:dvb followed by a namespace specific string, assigned by DVB and resolved through DVB-run catalogues and service discovery.
tldr.outcome: IANA registered dvb in the URN Namespaces registry. The RFC is Informational and was later updated by RFC 7354 and RFC 8553.

today: RFC 5328 is an Informational document that is updated by RFC 7354 and RFC 8553. Check those documents for the current rules.

sections.title: Why DVB Wants URNs
sections.content:
The Digital Video Broadcasting Project (DVB) describes itself as an industry-led consortium of over 270 broadcasters, manufacturers, network operators, software developers and regulatory bodies in over 35 countries, working on global standards for digital television and data services.

DVB wants unique, permanent, location-independent names, built as URNs under the syntax of RFC 2141, for resources it produces or manages. This document is the specification for a formal namespace, registered under the procedures of RFC 3406.
sections.plainLanguage: A web address says where a thing lives, and it breaks when the thing moves. A permanent name says what the thing is, wherever it lives.

sections.title: The urn:dvb Namespace
sections.content:
The registration template gives the Namespace ID dvb, version 1, dated 2007-02-28. Names have the form urn:dvb:<NSS>, where the Namespace Specific String follows the syntax in RFC 2141 and is case insensitive. The scope is global.

Only DVB, and authorities it designates, assign names, as part of developing DVB standards. DVB may delegate parts of its namespace. Uniqueness is guaranteed because DVB ensures through its standardization process that an assigned string is never reassigned, and DVB commits to keeping the named resources accessible and persistent.

The namespace identifies metadata that describes DVB multimedia and interactive services: XML schema files, classification schemes and identification systems. Two examples are given, and the RFC says they are not guaranteed to be real.
sections.plainLanguage: All the names start with urn:dvb, like every book in one library starting with the same room number. Only the librarians may add a new name, and a name is never reused.

sections.title: Resolving DVB Names
sections.content:
Resolving a name means finding where the resource is. DVB maintains URN catalogues that map assigned URNs to URLs. A URN is valid if it is in a catalogue. No single resolution mechanism is defined, because the target devices differ. Two client classes are covered: a broadcast set-top box with a receive-only connection, and a home network end device (HNED) such as an IPTV set-top box or networked TV.

Three ways to convey resolution information are named: cyclic broadcast of Resolution Authority Records (RAR) and Resolution Records (RR) in the TV stream, multicast of RRs over the DVBSTP protocol, and unicast RRs in answer to an HTTP GET /dvb/sdns request.

To bootstrap, a client by default joins the well-known multicast addresses and uses port 3937 (dvbservdsc) over TCP and UDP to get a Service Discovery and Selection (SD&S) record. Non-default entry points can be found through DNS SRV records (RFC 2782) under the name _dvbservdsc in the domain services.dvb.org, for example _dvbservdsc._tcp.services.dvb.org.
sections.plainLanguage: A name tells you what you want, but not where it is. DVB keeps phone-book style lists, and TV boxes can hear the list being announced or ask for it over the internet.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC adds no security considerations beyond those normally associated with URNs in general, which are described in RFC 1737, RFC 2141 and RFC 3406. DVB may give special meaning to certain characters in the Namespace Specific String, and any security issue from that is outside the scope.

When a name is resolved, the resource may need to be authenticated. Information about authenticating the name or the resource should travel separately from the URN, not inside it. The design of such resolution mechanisms is guided by RFC 2276 and will be published as DVB specifications.
sections.plainLanguage: The name is just a label. Proof that a thing is genuine should come in a separate note, not be hidden in the label.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The document defines the URN Namespace ID registration of dvb, and states that IANA has registered dvb in the URN Namespaces registry. Because DVB publishes international standards and has a well-defined compliance regime, the request is for a formal namespace rather than an informal one.
sections.plainLanguage: The big list-keeper wrote 'dvb' in the official list of name families, so nobody else can use it.
